subject: Post-call: Vela PoC recap — model candidates & quant trade study
messages:
From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.ai>
To: Ethan Cole <ethan.cole@vela.ai>
Cc: Jordan Price <jordan.price@vela.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-12T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call: Vela PoC recap — model candidates & quant trade study

Hi Ethan / Jordan,

Thanks again for the call earlier — good to align on primary goals (docs extraction + entity normalization at 250 qps peak, 2x latency target vs current in-house solution, and strict PII handling). Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can scope a short PoC: 

1) What we heard
- Primary inference path: document->structured JSON (few-shot + instruction tuning)
- Latency SLO: p95 < 150ms for single-document inference (avg tokens ~320)
- Cost target: reduce per-doc token cost by ~40% vs current managed endpoint

2) Recommended model candidates for the PoC (balanced quality vs throughput):
- Mistral-Instruct-16B (fp16 native) — strong instruction-following, good baseline for accuracy.
- Llama3-70B distilled variant (AWQ / 8-bit PTQ) — likely best fidelity for complex normalization but heavier compute.
- Falcon-40B-8bit-AWQ (fast on A100/4x instances) — optimistic throughput/cost balance.

3) Quantization options we suggest evaluating in the PoC (short trade study):
- AWQ (per-channel quant + activation-aware fine-tuning): minimal quality regression on instruction tasks, decent throughput uplift (1.8–2.4x) depending on kernel support.
- GPTQ (post-training quant): faster conversion, sometimes higher regressions on long-context entity tasks; throughput similar to AWQ if kernels available.
- FP8 emulation (mixed FP8 / FP16 kernels): potential for best latency but needs careful calibration; riskier on rare token generation.

4) Immediate next steps I propose:
- We upload a first prompt set (attached as vela_prompt_set_v1.txt) and a short eval harness — run 200 representative docs through L3-70B fp16 + Mistral-16B fp16 to capture baseline accuracy.
- Redwood will run a small quant tradeoff matrix (attached) converting 70B with AWQ and GPTQ and report quality deltas (EM / field-level F1) + throughput numbers on your target instance types.
- Proposed PoC timeline: 2 weeks for baseline + quant experiments, then one in-person review.

Attachments: vela_prompt_set_v1.txt (prompt variants + labels), vela_quant_tradeoff_matrix.xlsx (planned runs), vela_bench_results_summary.pdf (blank template).

Would you like us to start with Mistral-16B fp16 baseline first or run Mistral + L3-70B concurrently?

Best,
Nikhil
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Ethan Cole <ethan.cole@vela.ai>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jordan Price <jordan.price@vela.ai>
Date: 2027-05-12T16:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Vela PoC recap — model candidates & quant trade study

Thanks Nikhil — this is great and aligns with Jordan's notes. Quick answers:
- Please run Mistral-16B baseline and the L3-70B AWQ conversion in parallel if it's cheap to spin both up — we'd like a direct quality comparison.
- For infra, our dev cluster is A100-80GB (2x cards per node); we can give access to one node for the PoC.
- Priority metric: field-level F1 on entity normalization, with latency as a hard SLO.

Jordan + I will upload a sample of 500 annotated docs to the Drive link you shared by EOD tomorrow.

—Ethan
Director, ML Engineering
Vela.ai

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ethan Cole <ethan.cole@vela.ai>, Jordan Price <jordan.price@vela.ai>
Date: 2027-05-13T09:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Vela PoC recap — model candidates & quant trade study

Adding a few engineering notes from the infra side: 

- Throughput expectations (rough, based on Redwood internal runs + A100-80GB):
  * Mistral-16B fp16: ~280–320 qps for short context (avg 320 tokens) when properly batched; p95 latency target easily met with adaptive batching.
  * L3-70B AWQ: ~60–90 qps on a single 2x A100 node depending on KV cache usage; AWQ kernels give ~2x speedup vs naive 8-bit kernels in our tests.
  * Falcon-40B AWQ: ~120–160 qps; lower quality risk than GPTQ on instruction tasks in our limited evals.

- Quality regressions we've observed in prior PoCs: GPTQ conversions sometimes drop template-sensitive fields (dates, hyphenated IDs) — AWQ tended to preserve those better on instruction tasks. FP8 emulation can be unstable for tail-case tokens without extra calibration.

I'll queue the following runs on Redwood infra once we have the annotated sample: baseline fp16 runs (Mistral + L3-70B), AWQ(L3-70B) conversion + evaluation, GPTQ(L3-70B) conversion + evaluation. We will capture EM and field-level F1, plus token-level hallucination rates.

Marissa
Principal Engineer, Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Ethan Cole <ethan.cole@vela.ai>, Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-14T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Vela PoC recap — model candidates & quant trade study

Ethan — quick note on evaluation and anchors:

- Please include 40 hand-curated edge-case docs (we'll call them anchors) that capture messy OCR artifacts, nested tables, and unusual date formats. These are where quant methods tend to diverge.
- We'll report comparisons as deltas vs fp16 baseline: 
  * Accuracy delta (field-level F1)
  * Latency delta (p95)
  * Cost delta (estimated $/1000 docs)

- If you prefer, Redwood can run a paired A/B test across your sample so you can see token-by-token diffs in a shared report.

I'll attach a short eval script and the tradeoff matrix when I kick off the runs.

Thanks,
Soojin
Applied ML — Inference
Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Price <jordan.price@vela.ai>

Date: 2027-05-14T09:31:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Vela PoC recap — model candidates & quant trade study

Thanks team — we uploaded the 500 annotated docs plus the 40 anchor cases to the Drive folder (link in your HubSpot task). A couple quick asks: 

- Please prioritize the L3-70B AWQ run first if it's not materially more expensive — we want to know if AWQ preserves our normalization rules before we consider lighter-weight 40B variants.
- Can you capture example diffs for 10 docs where the quantized model changed tokenization/field boundaries? That will help our QA team triage.

Jordan
Head of Data Engineering
Vela.ai
